_about: Batch 2 (proposed 2026-10-16, waiting for approval): every instrument taught at Kashkoul Academy (oud, percussion: riq/daf/darbuka, violin, buzuq, guitar, piano, qanun, trumpet, ney, saxophone, clarinet), with several choices each (starter / step-up / better / kids) plus a few essentials. Researched on amazon.com 2026-10-16. kg = boxed shipping weight (Amazon's, or an estimate, see kg_source). our_price = round_up((amazon_price + kg × 15) × 1.2) − 0.01; the price at import time is what counts.

notes.oud-buzuq: Amazon US has thin choice for both instruments. OUD: no ouds under ~$359; almost every listing is from Sala Muzik (Turkish workshop, ships from Turkey as seller-fulfilled), and only two listings have more than ~10 reviews (AAO-108 and AO-101M, both $399). Mid-East Arabic Oud Sheesham (B00GBI1EHI, $499.89, 4.2/6 reviews, Amazon says 2.8 lb) is a possible extra but sheesham is a lesser tonewood and reviews are mixed; Mid-East walnut (B076HYRKBF, $509.52, 5.0/3, 3 left) is another. Electric/silent ouds exist ($699+) but have very few reviews. BUZUQ: no real buzuq with any reviews on Amazon US. The only true buzuqs are UNOSELL 'Arab Kurdish Buzuq' listings (B0DJGNG4QN $699.99, B0F672B3Z9 $799.99 with pickup) with zero reviews and 1 left each - not recommended without seeing one. All three buzuq picks are Turkish long-neck baglama/saz substitutes, which a teacher may need to re-fret/re-string for buzuq tuning. All listings are single (no variants). Oud weights: Amazon's 2 kg figures are instrument-only; boxed oud with soft case estimated at 3.2 kg (matches Amazon's 7 lb on AAO-108). No batteries in any pick. Saz-string set B0CP2K8XZ2 (LEYFA) was out of stock.
notes.qanun-ney: QANUN: Amazon US has no starter or mid-price qanun. Every real instrument is a handmade professional one at $1,199-$1,399, almost all from Sala Muzik (Turkish maker/seller, maker Mustafa Saglam, ships itself from Turkey). Only the MK-123 has meaningful reviews (4.6, 10). Sala's Arabic-setup MKA-4 is the better fit for Arabic maqam teaching in Lebanon but has no reviews yet. Also seen but not picked: Arabic 'Shami' qanun by Yasser Khadir (B0G8L7D6NK, $1,199, Ethnic Musical, no reviews, only 2 left). Skipped: B08K4L4YGT Saglam wenge kanun ($1,399, 3.3 from 3 reviews) and $2,600-$4,000 unreviewed listings. Qanun weights are estimates: Amazon's '5 kg' is the bare instrument, but it ships with a hard case. Qanun strings on Amazon are poorly reviewed (3.1) or have a single review, so none were picked. NEY: real cane neys come from two Turkish sellers, Ethnic Musical (Master Huseyin neys, key selectable) and Sala Muzik. Review counts are small everywhere. Skipped: Sala's cheapest $49 ney (B00NFR6XPQ, 4.0 from 49 reviews, with complaints about cracks and 'no sound') and the AKN-201 and other plastic singles rated 3.1-3.7. Cane neys can crack in dry or heated rooms, so tell students to oil them and store them in a case. None of the items have batteries. Amazon lists no weight for the neys, so all ney weights are estimates for a long thin box.
notes.percussion: Darbuka and daf choices are good. Riq is scarce on Amazon US: no credible starter-tier riq exists (cheap results are Western tambourines, not riqs; Bavly/MOP riqs at about $145-155 have zero reviews or are out of stock; Remo Riq $199 has only 2 reviews, a third-party seller and no reliable weight), so only 2 riq picks, both $249+ with few reviews and low stock. Weights marked estimate include box/case since Amazon lists bare-instrument or nonsense figures. Most picks ship from third-party sellers (SalaMuzik, The Eastern Bazzar, West Music) rather than Amazon; Gawharet El Fan and Meinl riq stock is very low. No darbuka bag recommended: listings are weak and the darbuka picks already include a bag/case.
notes.violin-guitar: Checked on amazon.com 2026-10-16. Ladders: Violin = Eastar set (existing, ~$126, starter; already has 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, full) -> Mendini MV500 (step-up) -> Bunnel Pupil (better); kids = Cecilio CVN-300 and Bunnel Pupil 3/4. Guitar = Yamaha C40II (existing, starter) -> Yamaha CG122MSH/CG102 family (step-up) -> Cordoba C5 (better); kids = Yamaha CGS family (1/2, 3/4, full) and Cordoba C1M (1/4 to full); MasterPlay 30in stays the cheapest kids option. Weights: Amazon lists bare-instrument weights for most guitars and impossible ones (16 oz) for some outfits, so boxed weights are estimated where flagged. The C40II in import-batch-1 uses 1.5 kg (bare guitar); its real boxed weight is probably about 2.5 kg, so it may be underpriced on shipping. Skipped: D'Addario Prelude violin strings (30 variants, over the limit) and Thomastik Dominant ($67, 17 variants) - if strings are wanted, Dominant is the better pick within budget. Stentor 1400/1500 listings mix 11 sizes from third-party sellers with low stock; Mendini MV300 rated 4.0 with 16 variants; Cordoba C3M had no price. All violin outfits on Amazon at these prices need a teacher's check of bridge, soundpost and pegs on arrival; Bunnel is the exception (set up by Kennedy Violins).
notes.piano: Ladder with the shop's existing items: kids 61-key (RockJam RJ5061 $130, Yamaha 61-key $200, new Casio CT-X700 with Arabic scales) -> budget 88 semi-weighted (Alesis Recital) -> budget 88 hammer (Yamaha P71, already in shop) -> step-up 88 hammer (Roland FP-10, Yamaha P-145) -> better (Yamaha P-225) -> optional home cabinet (Donner DDP-80, heavy). Yamaha P-145BT and P-225 sit in the SAME Amazon variation family (7 variants: P-145BT, P-143 bundle with stand+bench, P-225 black, P-225 white, P-225 deluxe bundle, P-45, P-525). Importing either listing pulls all 7, including the P-525 (~22 kg) and P-45 (same as P71), so import once and delete unwanted variants, or keep the P-143 bundle as the 'home set' option. Prices on Amazon in Oct 2026 are higher than older references (P-225 $769.99, FP-30X $649.99). Casio CDP-S110 was not found in stock; Kawai ES-120 rated only 4.0; Alesis Recital Pro MK2 rated 4.0 from 13 reviews; Roland FP-30X ($649.99, 4.6, 388 reviews, 14.8 kg, third-party seller Instrumentpro) and Casio CDP-S360 ($549.99, 4.7, 70 reviews, ~10.9 kg, seller Austin Bazaar) are fine alternates. Triple-pedal units skipped: FP-10 and P-145 only support a single sustain pedal. None of the picks has a built-in lithium battery (Alesis and Casio take optional D/AA cells, not included). Our-price formula used ceil((price + kg*15)*1.2) - 0.01.
notes.winds: Prices/ratings read from amazon.com on 2026-10-16 (Berkeley CA delivery). Glory Bb trumpet (B0BRGW215W, already in shop) sits at the trumpet starter tier next to Eastar; stocking both is redundant. True starters: Eastar trumpet, Glory/Eastar alto, Eastar clarinet (budget builds, fine for a trial year after a teacher checks setup). 'Teacher would actually be happy' tier: Jean Paul USA TR-330/TR-430, AS-400, TS-400, CL-300/CL-400 and the Yamaha student models (YTR-2330, YAS-280, YCL-255). Yamaha listings are sold by third-party resellers (K-Wind, ECOMADE ARENA) above US street price, possibly without Yamaha warranty. Skipped: Mendini by Cecilio (trumpet B00I8QJT78 $160, clarinet B005CXMOEU $140; ISO reputation), Glory clarinet (B09CN69WNX $100, 8 variants), Selmer Prelude/Buffet (few reviews or no price), Jupiter JTR700 ($899, 24 reviews). Weights: Amazon's figures for brass/woodwinds are often the bare instrument; estimates are boxed instrument in case.

products.title: Qanun finger rings (yüksük) set

products.title: Qanun plastic mizrap picks, pair
